day01: Day one of making my dream game.
So here's the idea. There's a little pond out in the woods.
It's full of salmon. Big, fat, shiny salmon.
And bears are obsessed with salmon. Like, they'll stand in a waterfall all day just waiting for one to jump in their mouth.
So you run the pond, you raise the fish, and a bunch of cute bears come over to eat.
I'm calling it The Bear Must Eat.
Right now it's literally just squares. I know, I know.
The brown one is a bear. And the orange one is me. Yeah, I put myself in the game.
First test. All the bear has to do is walk to the pond.
And then he just walked on the water? Bro.
So yeah, nothing has collision yet. Fun.
Fish are next. What fish should I add? Tell me in the comments.
day02: They're just little squares for now, but they swim around and they kinda look alive.
And when two happy fish bump into each other, you get a baby fish. I love it.
Then I changed one tiny line of code, and this happened.
Every single fish went to the corner. Why the *corner*?
Turns out I forgot to normalize one vector. One.
Fixed it. And now the pond fills itself back up.
day03: Day three. Five p.m. is rush hour in my game.
The office closes, and here they come...
every bear in town, running straight to the pond.
They cannonball in, grab a fish, and pay you a few coins.
This is the part I've been waiting for. It's so dumb, I love it.
There's no fish left. *Zero.* They ate the whole pond.
And now they're all just standing in the water like, where's the food?
Okay, I need to balance this. That's a problem for tomorrow.
day04: Day four. Time to fix the orange square. That's me, by the way.
Look at me. No face, no hat, nothing. I deserve better.
So I rebuilt myself, cube by cube.
Top hat. Monocle. Gold chain. Yeah, I gave myself a gold chain.
Then I gave myself way too many animations. No regrets.
Bye, square me. Thanks for your service.
day05: Day five. Let me show you the bears.
This is office bear. He walks, he eats, and he roars when he's hungry.
Then there's grandma bear, construction bear, and the CEO. The CEO tips the best.
Which one are you? Be honest.
And now the brown squares finally turn into real bears.
Look at them cannonballing into the pond. I could watch this all day.
Everything else is still squares though. That's tomorrow.
day06: Day six. My pond still looks like a spreadsheet.
So I drew the whole thing. Every single pixel.
Grass, trees, flowers, rocks, lily pads, and real fish.
Then I added day and night.
Night is my favorite. Moonlight, fireflies, super chill.
And this is the exact same pond from day one.
day07: Day seven. You guys have been leaving comments.
Someone asked for a banana fish. So okay, banana fish it is.
I drew it pixel by pixel. Brown spots, and the stem is the tail.
Then I put it in the game as a super rare egg.
It's a banana. It's also a fish. And honestly? It's beautiful.
And of course the bears eat it. They eat everything.
What should I add next? Comment it, I'll probably add it.
day08: Day eight, and you can finally build stuff.
Like a whole little restaurant around the pond.
Every piece lands with a little plonk and a puff of dust. So satisfying.
Tables, a barbecue, a jukebox, and a big neon sign.
And at five p.m. the bears actually sit down and eat there.
A tiny restaurant for bears. I'm so happy with this.
day09: Day nine. The game worked, but it felt kinda dead.
Comic words, squash and stretch, screen shake, coins, and way too many sound effects.
Which one would you rather play?
day10: Day ten. I finally made a title screen.
And yes, there's always a bear in the pond. Always.
Ten days ago, this was a brown square walking on water.
Thanks for following along, seriously. Should I keep going?
